evals.prompt: https://freertos.github.io/coreMQTT/v5.0.2/ — I need full documentation of this MQTT library. 1 markdown file per section (Overview, Design, Configuration, ...) which contains full text of all its child pages.
evals.expected_output: A directory of .md files, one per top-level documentation section of the coreMQTT v5.0.2 Doxygen site (Overview, Design, Configurations, Functions, Porting Guide, Timeouts, Transport Interface, Data types and Constants), each containing the Markdown content of all its child pages under --- / > Source: separators, with Doxygen chrome (Loading/Searching/No Matches/Generated by/version banner) stripped, headings as # / ##, code blocks as ``` fences, and links as absolute [text](https://...) references.
expectations: The skill ran scripts/ensure_venv.sh (or otherwise ensured html2text/beautifulsoup4 are available) before requesting Markdown output
The skill fetched and parsed navtreedata.js (Doxygen mode) rather than scraping index.html links
Output contains 7-9 .md files, one per navtree top-level section
02_Design.md contains the Design child-page text including 'Interfaces and Callbacks' and 'Keep-Alive' as Markdown headings
03_Configurations*.md contains all configuration macros incl. MQTT_PINGRESP_TIMEOUT_MS and LogDebug
No output file contains 'Loading', 'Searching', 'No Matches', or 'Generated by' lines
Code blocks are fenced: each output file has an even count of ``` fence lines
Relative links were rewritten to absolute URLs (https://freertos.github.io/... appears in link targets)
No non-breaking space (\xa0) characters remain in output files

evals.prompt: Convert the documentation at https://www.mkdocs.org/ into markdown files, one per page.
evals.expected_output: The skill detects this is not a Doxygen site (no navtreedata.js), falls back to crawl mode, and produces one .md per crawled page with MkDocs header/footer/nav stripped, real Markdown headings, and absolute links.
expectations: The skill used --mode crawl (or auto which fell back to crawl)
One .md file per page was produced (--per-page layout)
Output files do not contain the site nav menu or footer text
Output files use # / ## Markdown headings and [text](https://www.mkdocs.org/...) absolute links
Code fences are balanced (even count of ``` lines per file)
The tool respected a politeness delay between fetches

evals.prompt: I have a small hand-written HTML documentation site in /tmp/my_docs (index.html plus pages/*.html files with a shared header/footer). Dump all of it into a single markdown file.
evals.expected_output: The skill serves the local directory (or uses file:// page URLs), runs the tool in crawl mode with --flat, and produces one ALL_DOCS.md containing every page's Markdown under --- / > Source: separators, with the shared header/footer chrome removed.
expectations: The tool was run with --flat against the local site (local http server or file://)
ALL_DOCS.md contains every page found by the crawler
Each page is separated by a --- line with a > Source: link to its original file
Repeated header/footer chrome lines were stripped (via content detection or --strip)
Code fences are balanced and headings render as Markdown
The skill verified the output (grep for boilerplate, fence balance, page count) and reported a summary

evals.prompt: Convert https://freertos.github.io/coreMQTT/v5.0.2/ to plain text files — and I mean txt, not markdown, I want to grep them.
evals.expected_output: The skill runs the tool with --format txt (or --txt), producing the classic plain-text .txt layout with =-rule page headers, no Markdown syntax, tables as 'cell | cell' lines.
expectations: The tool was run with --txt / --format txt
Output files have .txt extensions and use the 78-char = header rule format
No Markdown artifacts (# headings, ``` fences, [link](url)) appear in output files
Boilerplate and chrome are stripped the same as in Markdown mode
